The story is exceptionally unified, with every detail in the first half setting up an emotional and narrative payoff in the second half. The mother's stubbornness and daily habits—walking nine blocks to the post office in the kiln-like heat, refusing to wear her straw hat, making up words in the crossword, and cheating at gin rummy—all directly drive the plot and characterization. Her refusal to respect the heat logically leads to her heatstroke on the walk to the post office. Furthermore, the objects introduced during the son's June visit (the crossword puzzle, the water glass on the windowsill, the straw hat, the rooster spoon rest, and the rummy score sheet) are all revisited at the end when he returns to the empty house. These recurring elements transform from humorous quirks into poignant symbols of her unspoken affection, her lonely routine, and the Inevitable passage of time, creating a deeply satisfying and harmonious whole.
